awd_titl_txt: Travel: NSF Student Travel Grant for 2025 ACM Symposium on Computer Science and Law (CS&Law'25)
awd_abstract_narration:
This grant supports student participation in the 4th Symposium on Computer Science and Law (CSLaw), sponsored by the Association for Computing Machinery (ACM), to be held March 25-27, 2025, in Munich, German. The event brings together computer scientists and law scholars and policymakers to discuss the latest research, developments, and trends in the developing intersection of Computer Science and Law. Students will attend invited talks, technical paper presentations, poster sessions, and panel discussions. The topics discussed include cybersecurity and privacy, and more generally, the legal aspects of computer and software technology in all aspects of society, which has become especially critical as societal functions and capabilities are increasingly relegated automation by computers and software. The symposium allows computer scientists and legal scholars to work together to solve problems that require their combined expertise. 

Computer science and law have long existed in parallel, with occasional overlaps in areas such as export controls. However, computer technologies are now performing functions for which people used to be responsible, and now that computers are taking over these functions, new legal frameworks are needed to deal with the new roles of automated systems, applications and agents. Legal and regulatory aspects need to be implemented correctly to meet new types of requirements in order for users (citizens) to be served effectively.

This award reflects NSF's statutory mission and has been deemed worthy of support through evaluation using the Foundation's intellectual merit and broader impacts review criteria.

por.por_cntn:
NSF grant 2510047 was a student-travel grant for the 2025 ACM Symposium on Computer Science and Law.  The 2025 ACM Symposium on Computer Science and Law took place at the University of Munich in Germany on March 25-27, 2025.  Because the funds were not exhausted in 2025, the remainder was used to support student travel to the 2026 ACM Symposium on Computer Science and Law.   The 2026 ACM Symposium on Computer Science and Law took place at UC Berkeley on Mar 3-5, 2026.  As required by NSF policy, all of the funds were used for students at US colleges and universities or for US persons who are studying abroad.  ACM’s symposium series in Computer Science and Law, in which the 2025 symposium was the fourth and the 2026 the fifth, has impact on a broad range of societal issues, ranging from online security and privacy to AI safety to Internet platform regulation to digital intellectual property protection. Students' participation in these symposia increases the chances that society’s approaches to these issues reflect a broad range of interests.  Attendance of students at both the 2025 and the 2026 symposia was boosted by this NSF grant, and many of the students sought out the PI at the conferences to express their thanks.  The proceedings of both symposia can be found at https://computersciencelaw.org/.
